details.summary: This is a fantastic, flavorful, and fast plant-based breakfast scramble. However, it requires a minor ingredient adjustment to match standard US package sizes so the reader isn't left with an awkward amount of leftover tempeh.

dimensions.feedback: The Southwestern flavor profile is coherent, blending earthy cumin and smoked paprika with fresh avocado, cilantro, and bright cherry tomatoes.
All ingredients are correctly listed and utilized in the cooking steps.
Excellent instructions. Cook times are given as ranges, visual and texture doneness cues are clear, and a mid-cook check is explicitly included to prevent sticking.
The ingredients and techniques neatly align with the stated Southwestern-inspired style.
A stovetop skillet scramble is the perfect, low-fuss method for crumbled tempeh and frozen vegetables.
Computed values accurately reflect the ingredients. The somewhat high saturated fat is a natural result of the large tempeh portion combined with avocado.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish's flavor, texture, and convenience without making any banned health claims.
A hearty, highly appealing, and incredibly fast plant-based breakfast option.

Delivers excellent fiber and complex carbohydrates. While the saturated fat exceeds the 5g ceiling, it is entirely acceptable here because it derives entirely from whole, heart-healthy plant sources (soybeans, avocado, and olive oil).
Zero added sugar, and the 40.2g of carbohydrate falls securely in the target window, sourced excellently from 100% whole-wheat tortillas and vegetables.
Hits the breakfast intent perfectly: it is a savory, fast, high-protein, high-fiber skillet that will keep blood sugar steady until lunch.

The recipe calls for 10 oz of tempeh, but standard US tempeh is sold in 8 oz blocks. Requiring 10 oz forces the reader to buy two packages and awkwardly store a 6 oz remnant. Fix: Reduce the tempeh to 8 oz (exactly 1 standard package). This resolves the practical annoyance, naturally lowers the saturated fat closer to the ceiling, and—with the whole-wheat tortillas—still provides enough total protein (~27g) to clear the 26g breakfast floor.

details.summary: This is an excellent, flavorful, and highly practical plant-based breakfast scramble. It leverages smart shortcuts like frozen vegetables and meets the cookbook's nutritional and culinary goals perfectly in under 20 minutes.

dimensions.feedback: The earthy, nutty flavor of tempeh works wonderfully with the classic Southwestern spices. The cherry tomatoes and avocado add a necessary fresh, acidic, and creamy balance.
Every listed ingredient is used in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients are introduced.
Excellent use of time ranges, a check time ('checking at 4 minutes'), and strong visual cues ('until any ice has evaporated', 'browned and aromatic', 'pliable').
The dish aligns perfectly with a Southwestern profile through the use of cumin, smoked paprika, cilantro, and tortillas.
A skillet scramble is the perfect method for browning tempeh and cooking off the excess moisture from the frozen vegetables.

The nutrition values are highly plausible for these quantities. The slightly elevated saturated fat warning stems naturally from the whole soybeans in the tempeh and the avocado, which are healthful whole-food sources.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish. The tone is encouraging and avoids any banned 'detox' or 'cure' terminology.
A very appetizing, savory, plant-based breakfast that feels substantial, flavorful, and filling rather than restrictive.
Perfectly on-profile. It offers a strong dose of plant-based protein, whole-grain carbohydrates, and heart-healthy fats without relying on heavy cheeses or refined grains.
Zero added sugar, and the whole-wheat tortillas deliver a high-quality, complex carbohydrate base that keeps the meal safely out of the keto zone and squarely in the target window.
Fits the breakfast chapter's goal perfectly: a savory, high-protein, fast meal designed to keep morning hunger away.
Easily executable in under 20 minutes from a cold start. Frozen vegetables are a great shortcut, and tempeh is reliably found in the produce section of standard supermarkets alongside tofu.
